nZ-aRK15xGU.title: 30 minute Arm Workout with Dumbbells
nZ-aRK15xGU.description:
Sign up for REFINE here 👉 https://www.kaleighcohen.com/login-register/

This awesome upper body combo will strengthen and define your biceps, triceps, and shoulders! This arm workout is structured with hypertrophy training in mind to help us develop our muscles! The goal is to work with a fairly heavy weight so that we can challenge our muscles to build strength, but we also have shorter rest periods so we will help increase muscular endurance as well! This strength session includes 3 rounds to focus on the individual muscle group, shoulders, biceps, and triceps,  finishing with round 4 a burner round that we work through each muscle group! I have also included a warm up to make sure we get everything nice and warm, but if you need a longer warmup, you can find a link for that below! As always, finish out with a stretch, and I have a link for a stretch below as well!

BICEPS, TRICEPS, & SHOULDERS DUMBBELL WORKOUT STRUCTURE AND EXERCISES
EQUIPMENT NEEDED
- DUMBBELLS - I used my 5kg, 7.5kg, and 10kg, dumbbells.
- EXERCISE MAT

OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT
- EXERCISE BOX, BENCH, OR A RAISED STURDY SURFACE

*Modifications, if you don’t have a box/chair, just do the exercise standing or on the ground.

ROUND 1 SHOULDER FOCUS
WORK: 35 REST: 20
3 exercises repeat 3 times in a horizontal format
- SEATED OVERHEAD PRESS
- SNOW ANGELS - PALMS OUT
- OPEN & CLOSE PRESS

ROUND 2 BICEP FOCUS
WORK: 35 REST: 20
4 exercises repeat 3 times in a horizontal format
- BICEP CURLS
- HAMMER CURLS
- SEATED CONCENTRATION CURL - RIGHT SIDE
- SEATED CONCENTRATION CURL - LEFT SIDE

ROUND 3 TRICEP FOCUS
WORK: 35 REST: 20
 3 exercises repeat 3 times in a horizontal format
- SEATED OVERHEAD TRICEP EXTENSION
- TRICEP PUSHUPS (ARMS IN NARROW, ELBOWS GO BACK, NOT OUT)
- DIPS ON BOX (keep bum close to box) *MOD - TRICEP KICKBACKS

ROUND 4 BURNER! You may want to use a slightly lighter weight because the work timer is longer! I went down a smidge and also made adjustments during the sets. This will help increase muscular endurance!
WORK: 60 REST: ONLY LONG ENOUGH TO SWITCH WEIGHT/EXERCISE
3 exercises repeat 1 time through 
- SHOULDER PRESS
- BICEP CURLS
- OVERHEAD TRICEP EXTENSION

As always focus on maintaining proper form and a full range of motion, work at your own pace, go heavy enough, challenge yourself, and of course, make the most of it!

Don't forget to complete a proper warm-up before each workout or check this 5-minute warm-up out here! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LKSC_KujZ4g

-GLp1J1PMe0.title: 30 Min TOTAL ARMS DUMBBELL WORKOUT | Shoulders, Biceps, Triceps + ABS
-GLp1J1PMe0.description:
Get ready for a 30 minute total arms workout using dumbbells, targeting your shoulders, biceps, and triceps, with added abs and core. This strength focused routine includes a full warm-up and cool-down, and follows a rotating structure: we complete 3 sets per muscle group, cycling through shoulders → biceps → triceps, then finish each round with core work.

This is a follow-along workout designed to help you build upper body strength and definition using controlled dumbbell exercises. You'll get stronger, more sculpted arms — no fluff, just real training.

👉 Grab a set of dumbbells, clear some space, and let’s Build together!

💡 Lifting Tips for Strength & Muscle:

• Use a challenging weight that allows you to complete all sets with good form, but not easily.

• Control each rep — no swinging or rushing through the movement.

• Pause at the peak of the contraction (especially on curls and triceps work) for extra time under tension.

• Keep your core engaged throughout to support your posture and protect your lower back.

⭐Form over weight: Choose a weight you can control without sacrificing good form.


Equipment Needed:

• A set of dumbbells (I used 9kg/20lbs & 12kg/26lbs)

• Optional mat

• Water + towel

SHOULDERS

30 minutes. Dumbbells only. Biceps and triceps from every angle. Ally's leading you through a full arm day you can do at home, at the gym, or anywhere you can grab a set of dumbbells.

Scaled for any level — go heavier or lighter, faster or slower. The work is the same. The results show up either way.

⏱️ DURATION: ~30 minutes
🏋️ EQUIPMENT: Dumbbells only (one moderate pair is enough)
📋 LEVEL: Beginner to advanced — scale by weight and tempo
💪 FOCUS: Biceps and triceps, with forearm work baked in

🎯 WHAT YOU'LL FEEL
- Biceps under tension from multiple angles (curls, hammer, incline)
- Triceps lit up from overhead, kickback, and skull-crusher patterns
- Real arm pump by the halfway point
- Grip and forearms working harder than you expected

💪 WHO THIS IS FOR
- Anyone wanting bigger, stronger arms without a full gym
- Lifters adding a dedicated arm day to their split
- Beginners learning curl and extension form with proper cues
- Travel and home gym warriors with limited equipment

🔥 HOW TO USE IT
- As your weekly arm day in a push/pull/legs or upper/lower split
- Added to the end of a back day (biceps) or chest day (triceps)
- Standalone on a busy week when you only have 30 minutes
- Beginners: 1x per week. Advanced: pair with a heavy push day.

📲 Want full programs that build your arms alongside strength, mobility, and conditioning every week? Trainer-led programming in the Gymn'i app — free 7-day trial.

q2VirW9zSBU.title: 40 MIN FULL BODY DUMBBELL WORKOUT | Intermediate Home Strength Training
q2VirW9zSBU.description:
Build strength, improve muscle definition, and train your entire body at home with this 40-minute full-body dumbbell workout. This intermediate workout combines lower-body, upper-body, chest, glute, and core exercises in one balanced training session.
We’ll begin with a dynamic warm-up to prepare your muscles, mobilize your joints, and gradually raise your heart rate. The main workout is divided into three sections:
- Lower-body strength for the glutes, quads, hamstrings, and calves
- Upper-body strength for the back, shoulders, biceps, and triceps
- Chest, glute, and core exercises performed on the mat
We’ll finish with a gentle full-body stretch to release tension, improve mobility, and bring your breathing back to normal.
WORKOUT DETAILS
- Total time: 40 minutes
- Fitness level: Intermediate
- Warm-up: 30 seconds work, 10 seconds rest
- Main workout: 45 seconds work, 15 seconds rest
- Cool-down and stretching included
- Equipment: One pair of dumbbells and an exercise mat
- No jumping and apartment-friendly
- Suitable for home or gym workouts
Choose a dumbbell weight that feels challenging while still allowing you to maintain proper form. You can use lighter weights for the upper-body exercises and heavier weights for the lower-body section.
This workout is ideal for anyone looking for a full-body strength workout, home dumbbell workout, muscle-toning workout, low-impact workout, or intermediate strength-training routine.
Remember to move at your own pace, stay hydrated, and stop if you experience pain or unusual discomfort.

4yiO5sfVWNc.title: 30 Min Full Body Dumbbell Strength Workout | Pregnancy-Friendly + Beginner-Friendly
4yiO5sfVWNc.description:
30 Min Full Body Dumbbell Strength Workout | Pregnancy-Friendly + Beginner-Friendly
#FullBodyWorkout #DumbbellWorkout #PregnancyWorkout #BeginnerWorkout #StrengthTraining

Ready to build strength from head to toe? 🤍 Join me for this 30-minute full-body dumbbell strength workout designed to help you strengthen your entire body with low-impact, beginner-friendly movements!
We'll work our legs, glutes, back, shoulders, arms, and core using controlled strength exercises that can be modified to meet you where you are. Whether you're pregnant, getting back into a fitness routine, or simply looking for a beginner-friendly full-body workout, this session is a great way to make time for yourself and keep building strength!

💪 WORKOUT DETAILS
Duration: 30 minutes
Equipment: Dumbbells (I used 10 lb and 15 lb weights)
Workout style: Full-body strength training
Level: Beginner-friendly
Impact: Low-impact, no jumping
Focus: Legs, glutes, back, shoulders, arms, and core

🤍 PREGNANCY-FRIENDLY WORKOUT REMINDERS
Every pregnancy and every body is different. Choose weights that feel appropriate for your current strength and energy level, take breaks whenever needed, and keep breathing throughout each movement. Avoid holding your breath or forcing your core to brace. Modify or stop any exercise that causes abdominal doming or coning, pelvic pressure, pain, dizziness, or discomfort. Please follow your healthcare provider's guidance about exercise during pregnancy.

Remember, you don't have to do every rep perfectly or lift the heaviest weights to make progress. Show up, listen to your body, and celebrate what you can do today! 🥰

👇 LET'S CONNECT!
Did you work out with me today? Leave a comment below and let me know how you felt! I love hearing from you and cheering you on throughout your strength journey.

If you enjoyed this workout, please LIKE this video, SUBSCRIBE to Strength by Amanda, and turn on notifications so you don't miss our next workout together!

Looking for more workouts? Check out my 14-Day Stronger Mom Challenge and the next workout linked on your end screen. Let's keep building strength together, one workout at a time! 🤍💪🏼

Npm2PHZXs68.title: 20 MIN Full Body Dumbbell Workout | Beginner to Intermediate
Npm2PHZXs68.description:
Join me for a 20-minute full body dumbbell workout at home, followed by a cooldown and stretch. This low-impact, no-jumping session combines lower-body exercises, upper-body strength work, and a core finisher in one follow-along workout.

Workout level: Beginner to Intermediate.

Workout format: No repeat.

We’ll move through squats, lunges, rows, presses, and deadlifts before heading to the mat for chest, glute, and core work. Finish with plank T rotations and a final plank hold, then take a moment to slow down and stretch.

This session is best suited to beginners with some familiarity with dumbbell exercises through intermediate exercisers. Choose weights that let you move with control, follow your own pace, and take extra breaks whenever you need them.

YOU’LL NEED
• A pair of dumbbells
• An exercise mat for the floor section
• Water and enough space to move comfortably

MAKE IT YOUR OWN
Use lighter weights or try the movements without weights while learning the technique. For the plank section, lower your knees or hold a modified plank instead of rotating.

The main workout lasts 20 minutes. The intro and cooldown are additional. Take a few minutes to warm up before starting.

evg4roIn0yI.title: 16: No Repeat Dumbbell Burn Workout | 30-Min Strength + Cardio, No Intervals | BodyFit By Amy
evg4roIn0yI.description:
🔥 No Repeat Dumbbell Burn Workout | Full Body Strength + Cardio | No Intervals, No Clock | BodyFit By Amy | 30 Mins

No repeats, no intervals, no stress. This full-body workout runs in four 5-minute blocks — lower body, upper body, core, and a compound finisher — with no timer popping up to tell you what's coming next. Every exercise flows into the next, building unilateral work and muscle endurance without the pressure of watching a clock. Just trust your body and keep moving.

Dumbbells only — use whatever sets you've got, building from one weight to two as each block develops.

✅ Total body: legs, glutes, hamstrings, back, shoulders, biceps, triceps & core
✅ Four 5-minute blocks, no intervals or timed rest — pure flow
✅ Dumbbells only
✅ Builds from single-weight unilateral work to bilateral compound moves
✅ The most core work of any BodyFit by Amy format — a full 5-minute block
✅ Bonus 60-second power finisher — snatch + mountain climber
✅ All fitness levels — modifications throughout

➡️ HOW THIS WORKOUT WORKS:
Four 5-minute blocks, each building without a clock to watch:
🦵 LOWER BODY — single-weight unilateral work building to compound squat-lunge combos
💪 UPPER BODY — single-arm row building to biceps, chops & reverse fly
🎯 CORE — the full block, from march to dead bug to side plank to body saw
🔥 COMPOUND FINISHER — deadlift/row, plié squat, triceps/bridge — everything together
The result? Real muscle and cardio endurance without the mental weight of counting down intervals — just listen to your body and keep going.

➡️ WORKOUT STRUCTURE
4 Five-Minute Blocks + Bonus Finisher

Block 1 — Lower Body:
Goblet Squat (single weight) → Side Lunge (single weight) → Squat + Side Lunge Combo → Kickstand Deadlift → Curtsy Lunge → Squat + Lunge Combo

Block 2 — Upper Body:
Single-Arm Row → Alternating Bicep Curl → Overhead Tricep Extension → Bicep Curl → Standing Chop (right & left) → Reverse Fly

Block 3 — Core:
March → Toe Tap → Dead Bug → Overhead Sit-Up → Slow Bicycle → Hollow Hold → Side Plank Lift (right & left) → Side Plank Twist (right & left) → Plank Knee Tap + Twist → Body Saw

Block 4 — Compound Finisher:
Deadlift + Bent-Over Row → Reverse Lunge (both legs) → Plié Squat + Circle → Lying Triceps + Bridge Lift → Leg Lower + Chest Fly

Bonus Finisher — Snatch + Mountain Climber (60 sec)

QrRDpD8xZfo.title: 🔥 30-Min Full Body Strength! 🔥 Build Muscle & Burn Fat | Menopause-Friendly Dumbbell Workout
QrRDpD8xZfo.description:
30-minute menopause strength workout designed for women over 50! Perfect for beginners, this routine will help you boost your metabolism, burn fat, and enhance vitality. With seven effective dumbbell exercises repeated three times, you'll work towards maintaining muscle mass and building strength, all from the comfort of your home.

✅KEEP GOING WITH THE  14 DAY LOSE BELLY FAT CHALLENGE  ✅
https://courses.fabulous50s.com/14-day-lose-belly-fat-challenge/

Weight training benefits for women going through menopause. 
1. Preserves Muscle Mass
Menopause-related muscle loss: During menopause, estrogen levels drop, which can lead to a loss of muscle mass and strength. Weight training helps maintain and even increase muscle mass, counteracting this natural decline.
Prevents sarcopenia: This is the age-related loss of muscle, and strength training is one of the most effective ways to slow it down or reverse it.
2. Improves Bone Health
Increases bone density: Post-menopausal women are at higher risk of osteoporosis due to a reduction in estrogen, which affects bone density. Weight-bearing exercises like strength training help stimulate bone growth, reducing the risk of fractures and osteoporosis.
Prevents fractures: Stronger bones are less likely to break, particularly in critical areas like the hips, spine, and wrists.
3. Boosts Metabolism
Increases resting metabolic rate: Muscle is more metabolically active than fat, meaning the more muscle mass you have, the more calories you burn at rest. This helps counter the slower metabolism that often accompanies menopause, assisting in weight management.
Helps with fat loss: Weight training can promote fat loss and help prevent the common post-menopausal weight gain, especially around the abdomen.
4. Enhances Mental Health
Reduces anxiety and depression: Menopause can bring emotional changes due to fluctuating hormones. Strength training can improve mood by increasing the production of feel-good hormones like endorphins and serotonin.
Improves sleep: Regular weight training can promote better sleep patterns, which are often disrupted during menopause due to night sweats or insomnia.
5. Supports Joint Health
Improves joint flexibility and mobility: Strengthening the muscles around joints helps stabilize and protect them, potentially reducing joint pain and stiffness.
Reduces risk of arthritis: Weight training keeps joints flexible and helps maintain a full range of motion, which can reduce the onset or severity of arthritis.
6. Balances Hormones
Regulates insulin and glucose: Weight training can help improve insulin sensitivity, reducing the risk of type 2 diabetes, which becomes more common during and after menopause.
Supports hormonal balance: Although estrogen levels drop, weight training encourages the production of other beneficial hormones like growth hormone and testosterone, which help preserve muscle mass and metabolic function.
7. Boosts Cardiovascular Health
Lowers blood pressure: Regular resistance training helps improve circulation and can reduce blood pressure, lowering the risk of heart disease, which increases after menopause.
Improves cholesterol levels: Strength training can raise HDL (good cholesterol) and lower LDL (bad cholesterol), supporting heart health.

wLtlY8WKDIE.title: 20 min KETTLEBELL FULL BODY HIIT WORKOUT | Follow Along
wLtlY8WKDIE.description:
🔥 20-Min Full Body Kettlebell Workout – EMOM Style for Fat Loss & Conditioning

Hey athletes! Today we’re doing a high-intensity kettlebell EMOM workout designed to smash your full body, boost endurance, and light up your calorie burn.

We’ve got 3 spicy rounds, 6 minutes each, with 90 seconds rest between. Each minute starts with a set number of reps – then you rest the remainder. Simple… but not easy 😮‍💨

You’ll need just one kettlebell – something you can shoulder press for 10 reps per side. I’m using a 24kg bell and will absolutely regret it by the end (spoiler: I die on the floor).

⸻

💥 EMOM Workout Breakdown (20 min total):

Min 1: 10 Thrusters (Left)
Min 2: 10 Thrusters (Right)
Min 3: 10 Goblet Clean Squats
Min 4: 10 High Pulls (Both Hands)
Min 5: 10 Burpees
Min 6: 20 Russian Swings
Min 7: REST 🧎‍♂️

→ Repeat 3 rounds

-

Guide & Tips:

👉🏻 Start SLOW!

I can’t emphasize this enough: your first round shouldn’t feel too hard, if it is, you're gonna have a hard time finishing the workout, especially in the longer EMOM’s

👉🏻 What about a warmup?

I usually start an 8-minute timer and do 3 quick rounds of 10 swings, 10 air squats, 10 pushups (which takes like, 3-4 minutes), then stretch in the remaining time.

👉🏻 What weight should I use?

Pick a weight you can shoulder press around 8-12 times on each shoulder from the rack position.

👉🏻 What weight do you use?

I believe in the minimalistic approach, and I’m using a 24kg (52lbs) kettlebell for 99% of my workouts. recently introduced a new 32kg, but you won’t find it in my workout follow-along videos 😅.

👉🏻 What’s an EMOM?

Stands for ‘Each Minute On the Minute’, perform a set number of reps in the beginning of each minute and rest until the end of the minute

👉🏻 Why EMOM?

Because EMOM kettlebell workouts are 🔥, they keep you laser-focused with no time to slack off, push your intensity through the roof, build real strength and cardio endurance at the same time, are easy to follow with just a timer, and super time-efficient - you can get an insane full-body session in half the time without overthinking a thing.

- DUMBBELLS- I used a range from 10lbs to 20lbs / 4.5-9kg When selecting a weight for this workout, you want to lift moderately heavy!

6 SUPERSETS (EACH SUPERSET WILL FOCUS ON THE SAME MUSCLE GROUP- BICEPS, TRICEPS, OR SHOULDERS)

Let's tone & strengthen our arms with this no repeat 35 minute biceps and shoulders home workout with dumbbells.  

➡️ please use the links below to shop my workout clothes & equipment

We will be completing this workout in two parts.  In the first part, we will be completing unilateral (one arm at a time) movements, and we will be going for 30 seconds of work & 15 seconds of rest.  In the second part, we will be completing alternating (one arm, then the next in the same set) movements, and we will be going for 40 seconds of work & 20 seconds of rest. I will be using 2 x 10 lbs dumbbells for most of the exercises, and an 18 lbs dumbbell/kettlebell for some of the alternating arm exercises at the end.  The timer is just a guide: please take breaks when you need them.  Remember to keep your core tight for max effect.  I also recommend keeping your knees slightly bent for better stability.

HlnCRJ2Z-i8.title: 30 Minute Full Body Dumbbell Strength Workout | Intense Muscle Sculpt Grind
HlnCRJ2Z-i8.description:
Take your muscular endurance and strength to the next level with this 30 minute full body workout, an intense grind session designed to sculpt, tone, and strengthen your entire physique. Focused on strength with dumbbells, this targeted routine combines high-tension compound lifts and core controls, giving you the perfect high-calorie burn without needing a gym. If you're looking for an effective 30 minute cardio workout with weights, this dumbbell workout is engineered for maximum muscle activation.

We launch this strength flow targeting the lower body and glutes with a dynamic walking goblet squat, alt curtsy lunges + back extensions, isolated single-leg R & L leg hip thrusts, a crunch hold alt heel touch, and a stabilizing plank hold. The upper body and chest kick in with a hip thrust hold + press, sit-up hold, biceps + overhead press, and weighted squats.

The core and upper body burnout deepens with a low push-up hold, hip thrust hold + alt chest press, squat + alt back lunges, and weighted over leg bicycle crunches. We fire up the legs again through L & R lunge pulses, alt front lunges with weight, and a heavy deadlifts + alt back lunges combo.

To wrap up this ultimate full body workout, we finish strong with walking pushups, single-leg Romanian deadlifts (R & L), targeted biceps curls, low triceps extensions, a plank hold + alt triceps isolation, and weighted sit-ups. No talking—just a pure 30 min hiit strength follow-along for all fitness levels. Grab your dumbbells and let’s work !

Get ready to strengthen your arms, chest, back, shoulders and abs! This 30 Minute Upper Body Dumbbell Workout is designed to help you build muscle, improve strength, and feel amazing—all from the comfort of your home! Grab your dumbbells and follow along as we target every major muscle group in your upper body during this dumbbell upper body workout!

Whether you're a man or women, beginner or more advanced, this upper body dumbbell and abs workout is structured to help you push your limits and see results.

The Importance of Diet and Exercise
Exercise is only part of the equation when it comes to achieving your fitness goals. Pairing a consistent upper body workout routine with a well-balanced diet is key to building strength and improving overall health. Prioritize whole, nutrient dense foods like lean proteins, complex carbs, healthy fats, and plenty of vegetables. Staying hydrated and getting enough rest are equally important to support muscle recovery and energy levels.

🔥 Tips for Reaching Your Fitness Goals:
1️⃣ Set Realistic Goals: Start with small, achievable goals and track your progress over time.
2️⃣ Be Consistent: Regular workouts and a steady routine are more effective than sporadic intense sessions.
3️⃣ Fuel Your Body: Proper nutrition powers your workouts and aids in recovery. Don't skip meals or over-restrict.
4️⃣ Progressive Overload: Gradually increase the weight or intensity to challenge your muscles and promote growth.
5️⃣ Stay Positive: Fitness is a journey! Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and stay committed.

nudaLbELR5A.title: SLOW DOWN Shoulders Dumbbell Workout // The Shoulder Workout You Didn't Know You Needed // 25 Min 💪
nudaLbELR5A.description:
Fire 🔥🔥 shoulder work!!    Working with dual sets today adding that extra tension on the muscle to fully fatigue it and create change.  I am using 2 sets of dumbbells, (2 x 15lbs, 2 x 8lbs), but feel free to use whatever you have access to.  This workout is all about controlling the weight while lifting and lowering as opposed to swinging the weights.  Put extra control into the lowering phase and try to slow it down a bit.

Strength training can be accessible to any fitness level, just move your body!  You can do this workout with any household item that has weight to it such as soup cans, take it slower or omit some moves if they cause pain.  If you ever feel pain, stop!  Discomfort, shaking and possible swearing may occur but pain is a full stop! 

The format today will be 45 seconds work of intentionally slowed down effort followed by an additional 30 seconds work at a regular pace and 30 seconds rest.  If you need additional time to set up and ensure correct form, please take it!  The timer is simply there to keep us on track.  It is not an end all be all.  Take the time to lift the weights with control, move your body as it will allow, take necessary breaks to reset, and smile!! 😁

#strengthworkout #strength  #shoulderworkout   #shoulderstrength #dumbbell  #dumbbellworkout #musclestrength #strongshoulders   #athomeworkout

J2Z-OcVCOvI.title: 42 Min Upper Body & HIIT Workout: Build Muscle at Home
J2Z-OcVCOvI.description:
This is a follow-along strength and HIIT session you can do in your living room. All you need is a pair of dumbbells and a little floor space.
We focus on arms, shoulders and upper back, with two short HIIT blocks to raise your heart rate and work your legs. You’ll build strength, burn energy and finish feeling stronger than when you started.

HOW THE WORKOUT IS SET UP
Strength blocks: 40 seconds of work, 20 seconds of rest, 2 rounds
HIIT blocks: 30 seconds of work, 10 seconds of rest, 2 rounds
The timer runs on screen, so just press play and follow along.

Build strength and burn energy with this 42-minute dumbbell workout. A structured follow-along session for your living room.

This session is Week 4, Workout 1 of my home series, focusing on your arms, shoulders, and upper back. It combines dedicated lifting blocks with high-intensity intervals, making it ideal for busy individuals who need a smart, efficient routine. You will need a pair of dumbbells, a mat, and some floor space to move.

Regular strength training is essential for maintaining bone density and joint health as you age. By alternating between lifting and a quick HIIT session, we keep your heart rate up and ensure the entire 42 minutes remains productive. If you are looking for sustainable fitness over 40, this routine helps you build muscle and stamina without needing a commercial gym.

Subscribe for a new home workout every week. Tell me in the comments which block was the hardest for you today!

CHAPTERS
0:00 Intro
00:10 Warmup
03:15 Block 1: Upper Body
15:14 Block 2: HIIT
22:11 Block 3: Shoulders + Arms
34:48 Block 4: HIIT

BLOCK 1 – UPPER BODY (12 min)

Arnold Press
Bent Over Row
Alternating Lateral Raises
Chest Press + Fly
Renegade Row
Pullover

BLOCK 2 – HIIT (6:40)

High Knees
Mountain Climbers
In & Out Squats
Butt Kicks
Skaters

BLOCK 3 – SHOULDERS + ARMS (12 min)

Alternating Shoulder Press
Upright Row
Single-Arm Bent Over Row + Tricep Kickback (Right)
Single-Arm Bent Over Row + Tricep Kickback (Left)
Alternating Bicep Curls
Overhead Tricep Extension

BLOCK 4 – HIIT (6:40)

High Knees
Mountain Climbers
In & Out Squats
Butt Kicks
Skaters

WHY THIS WORKOUT WORKS
Strength training is one of the best things you can do as you get older. It protects your muscles, supports your bones and joints, and gives you more energy for daily life. Short bursts of HIIT between the strength blocks help your heart and keep the session moving, so 42 minutes goes fast.

Go at your own pace. If a move doesn’t feel right, use lighter weights or slow it down. To make the HIIT gentler, march in place instead of jumping. Showing up every week matters more than going all-out once.

lMhDB_naNBY.title: Dumbbell Complex Workout // 25 Minutes Full Body Circuit At Home
lMhDB_naNBY.description:
DUMBBELL COMPLEX WORKOUT - 25 MINUTES FULL BODY CIRCUIT AT HOME // Today we are completing a dumbbell complex. 4 rounds of it, with 30 second recoveries in between each round. There will be 7 dumbbell complex exercises to complete in a back-to-back format and you cannot put the weights down until you have completed the entire round. Complexes are great for working on muscle endurance, burning fat and ramping up your metabolism. The dumbbell complex format is a very effective and time-efficient way to train.
 
We start with some RDL's and please make sure that your form is crisp on these. Brace your abs, hinge at your hips and use your glutes and hamstrings to extend back up to a standing position. Keep a tight position on your torso throughout the exercise, making sure that you protect your spine and lower back, moving within a safe range that is right for you. We then hit out some power work on the DB push presses overhead and focus on springing the weight from the hips and forcing the weight overhead in a strong, powerful but controlled manner. Onto some alternate arm, bent-over rows for 45 seconds and really focus on squeezing through your lats, maintaining a nice long spine and never rounding or arching your back. Keep your spine in a safe position always. Fifteen seconds of rest follow, where you will be breathing harder and need the oxygen but please do not put the weights down on the floor. Hold onto them all the time, until the entire first round is over.
 
We then have some alternate arm shoulder presses with a hammer grip, which I find easier on the shoulder joint. And then onto some DB deadlifts, where you need to again keep your torso tight and work on getting a nice, smooth hip drive going on. You want to be loading your hips on these, not your lower back. Straight into some bent-over rows with both arms and then another 15 second of rest, keeping the weights in your hands. 
 
We then finish on a hammer bicep curl into a 3-second pause front squat. Now, by the time I got to the 3rd and 4th round of these I had to switch the hammer curl out for a DB clean to get the weights onto my shoulders. My arms were getting too tired, as the weights were reasonably heavy for this workout. So, absolutely fine to go for a DB clean and then into a 3-second pause front squat afterwards. Sometimes, you need to improvise and change things up at the last-minute and I personally underestimated how tired my biceps would be on this particular exercise after all the previous exercises as well. So, just be pre-warned on that before starting the video.
 
What follows is a 30-second rest and make sure you sip some water and focus on your breathing and getting as much oxygen into your lungs as possible. The accumulative effect of this session will creep up on you in the 3rd or 4th round, provided you are using decent weights so just be sure to make use of every second of recovery to help your muscles push through with the work.
 
Good luck.

MZzAxivUZBI.title: 25 Min  🔥 Full Body Dumbbell Complex Workout | Beginner Strength  | I'VE GOT NO TIME Day 11
MZzAxivUZBI.description:
25 MIN 🔥 Full Body Dumbbell Complexes | Beginner Strength | Follow Along | Day 11 of 24 - . Grab your dumbbells!

DAY 11/24 of the I'VE GOT NO TIME Beginner Series: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLboRWRlNED7g

WORKOUT DETAILS
📌 Duration: 25 Minutes.
📌 Intensity: Burning 🔥🔥🔥
📌 Fitness Level: Beginner (everyone welcome 😊).
📌 Follow Along with cues and form tips.
📌 Equipment: 2 dumbbells + a mat.
📌 Rep based, not timed. 5 complexes × 10 reps, 4 rounds, 30 sec rest between rounds. Go at your own pace.

Hey GO-GETTERS, welcome back! Day 11 of I'VE GOT NO TIME is full body complexes, and it's the first rep-based workout in the series. No clock on the moves. You do 10 good reps, then move on.

A complex is two exercises joined into one rep. Sumo squat, then straight into a sumo RDL. Front rack squat, then straight into a shoulder press. Forward lunge, then a bicep curl. That's why it's such an efficient way to train when you have no time: every rep hits your legs, your core and your upper body together, and you're never standing around between exercises. Four rounds of five complexes and you've trained everything.

Pick a weight you can press overhead for 10 reps with good form. The last two reps of each set should be hard, not impossible. If you need to pause the video between rounds, pause it. Press play and move with me.

Do this warm-up before the workout: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EhTSF3YmqEQ&t=43s
Do this cool-down after the workout: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kB62jKi0ZRU&t=88s

▶ PRONE TO REVERSE GRIP BENT OVER ROW

q7RmB9YZvwQ.title: Pull Day Progress | Final Week at This Gym
q7RmB9YZvwQ.description:
This workout marks the final week training at this gym, with a new program and new environment starting next week. In this video, I talk through how I’ll be approaching that transition — how I’ll assess movements, build the next program, learn what works, and then progress it over time. Training isn’t just about following a plan blindly. It’s about thinking, adjusting, and refining as you go.

This pull day landed in Week 3 of my maintenance / diet break phase, and while all lifts progressed and execution stayed solid, I could definitely feel some fatigue creeping in. That fatigue might be coming from packing and moving, or it could simply be a reminder that I may need to eat before this session to better support performance. Either way, the session was still enjoyable — and that’s an important reminder: even when energy is lower, consistency and intent still matter.

The focus of this workout was a complete back and biceps hypertrophy session, targeting upper back, lower traps, upper lats, lower lats, rear delts, side delts, and arms. Exercise order, grip choice, and machine selection were all intentional — designed to build muscle, improve mind-muscle connection, and keep progression moving forward during a maintenance phase.

As I prepare to move gyms and start a new program, this session represents a checkpoint. What’s working? What needs refining? What movements feel best for my structure? These are the same questions every lifter should be asking if long-term muscle growth is the goal.

💥 PULL DAY HYPERTROPHY WORKOUT – WEEK 3 MAINTENANCE PHASE

Single-Arm Cross-Body Cable Lateral Raise – Extra side delt volume, trained first while fresh

Kelso Shrugs – Trap pre-fatigue to improve upper-back engagement

Chest-Supported T-Bar Row – Upper-back thickness and mid-trap focus

Plate-Loaded Low Row – Angled to bias a higher portion of the traps

Single-Arm Plate-Loaded Row – Upper-lat-focused compound pulling

Narrow MAG Grip Pulldown – Lower-lat bias with stretch and control

Superset: Machine Preacher Curl → Rear Delt Cable Fly – Time-efficient arm and rear-delt volume

🎯 SESSION THEMES

Progressing lifts even when energy isn’t perfect

Executing with intent over chasing load

Learning how fatigue affects performance

Preparing mentally and physically for a new program

Staying consistent during transitions

📈 MINDSET TAKEAWAY

Training won’t always feel perfect — but progress doesn’t require perfect conditions. Showing up, executing well, and reflecting honestly is what builds momentum. This phase is about learning, adapting, and carrying that forward into the next chapter.

❓ QUESTION OF THE DAY

What’s your favourite cereal? 🥣
Comment below — I want to hear it.
